chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Zarif, from Abi Hamzah:

For the wound that exposes the bone there are five camels; and for the simhaq, below the mudihah, there are four camels. For the munaqqilah there are fifteen camels, a tenth and a half of a tenth. As for the ja'ifah, which penetrates into the body cavity, there is no qisas in it, only assessed compensation. And the munaqqilah is that from which the bones are displaced, and there is no qisas in it, only assessed compensation. As for the ma'mumah, there is no fixed assessed compensation for it. The ma'mumah is a blow that lands on the head: if it is from a sword, then it cuts through everything and cuts the bone, reaching the struck person’s brain; and sometimes his tongue becomes heavy, and sometimes his hearing becomes heavy, and sometimes confusion overtakes him. And if he is struck with a pillar or with a severe staff, then it reaches even more intensely than cutting; from it the skullcap is broken, the skullcap of the head.

key_terms.اَلسِّمْحَاقِ: a wound less severe than the mudihah, reaching the thin membrane over the bone
key_terms.اَلْجَائِفَةِ: a penetrating wound that reaches the inner body cavity
key_terms.اَلْحُكُومَةُ: assessed compensation determined judicially where no fixed amount applies
key_terms.اَلْقِحْفُ: the skullcap or bony covering of the head
key_terms.اَلْمَأْمُومَةُ: a severe head wound reaching toward the brain
key_terms.اَلْمُنَقِّلَةِ: an injury in which the bones are displaced or moved from their place
key_terms.اَلْمُوضِحَةِ: a head wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: retaliatory legal retribution for an injury

ai.seo_question: What are the diya and qisas rulings for head wounds like al-mudihah, al-simhaq, al-munaqqilah, al-ja'ifah, and al-ma'mumah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal compensation rulings for different categories of wounds to the head and body, specifying amounts of blood-money and clarifying where qisas does not apply. It also defines technical injury terms such as al-munaqqilah, al-ja'ifah, and al-ma'mumah, describing the severity and bodily effects of such injuries within the framework of Islamic legal assessment.
